attack_plan.narrative: On March 24th, the Germanwings Airbus A320, flight number 4U9525, tragically crashed in the French Alps near Digne. Initial reports suggest that the aircraft was lost from radar near the region around 11:00 AM local time. Despite extensive search efforts, no survivors were found, and the debris of the aircraft was located at an altitude of approximately 2,000 meters. The flight path data reveals a sharp descent, raising immediate concerns about the circumstances leading to the crash. The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, was last seen in his apartment in Cologne just days prior to the incident, and authorities have noted the absence of definitive records regarding his mental health status during this period. This lack of information has led investigators to consider the possibility that Lubitz may have experienced a serious depressive episode or burnout that impacted his ability to perform his duties.
